title: Political participation is segmented into distinct access and meaning routes
source_unit: CPS Voting and Registration Supplement respondent, November 2024

reported_voting_advanced_degree.unit: percent of citizens with advanced degree

reported_voting_high_school.unit: percent of citizens with high-school education

observations.method: Census published CPS Voting and Registration Supplement estimates for the November 2024 presidential election. The denominator is represented as a 100-point published-rate base because the committed layer records rates rather than the full table's absolute citizen population count.
observations.uncertainty: Survey estimates can differ from administrative data or exit polls because of nonresponse, vote misreporting, wording, and survey administration; no interval is reproduced in this record.
observations.subgroup: Citizen voting-age population, with sex and education conditioning.
observations.counterinterpretation: Turnout and registration are not one measure of political engagement, and subgroup differences do not identify whether resources, time, health, place, identity, or institutions caused them.

observations.method: Census published Table 10 distribution of self-reported reasons for not voting among reported nonvoters age 18+.
observations.uncertainty: Published survey percentages; no formal contrast test is reproduced. Reasons are self-reported and categories are not a mutually exclusive causal model of nonparticipation.
observations.counterinterpretation: Schedule, illness, registration, transport, interest, and candidate dissatisfaction are distinct routes; they must not be summed into a single disengagement or apathy score.

boundary: This is a 2024 CPS voting and registration population layer. It does not follow respondents over time, identify a prior material or institutional trigger, measure trust or political meaning directly, or establish a causal path from cost, work, care, health, mobility, or administration to voting. The retrieval hash covers the committed analysis memo.
